stories.title: Deadly Earthquake Strikes Colombia, Causing Widespread Destruction
stories.summary: A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, resulting in at least 132 fatalities and over 570 injuries. The quake, described as the country's strongest in years, led to significant destruction, with many buildings collapsing and rescue efforts underway to find survivors. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency shortly after taking office, and the European Union is providing support for rescue operations.

stories.title: Syrian Court Sentences Bashar al-Assad to Death in Absentia for War Crimes
stories.summary: A Syrian court has sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the country's civil war. The ruling also included their cousin Atef Najib, who was present at the trial. The court's decision follows a lengthy conflict that has resulted in approximately half a million deaths.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike on Russian Oil Refinery Claims 13 Lives
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on the Taneco oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Russia, has resulted in the deaths of at least 13 people and injuries to 78 others. This attack, which occurred deep inside Russian territory, is reported to be one of the deadliest since the onset of the war. The strike is part of Ukraine's ongoing campaign to target critical infrastructure far from the frontline.

stories.title: Zelenskyy Reports Russian Strikes with North Korean Missiles in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that recent Russian missile strikes in Zaporizhzhia involved North Korean missiles, resulting in at least six fatalities and numerous injuries. He has raised concerns about the growing military collaboration between Russia and North Korea, particularly since 2024. Additionally, reports indicate that overnight attacks across Ukraine have left at least nine people dead and many more wounded.

stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Claims Over 2,000 Lives, Marked as Fastest Growing on Record
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo reports that at least 2,000 people have died in its ongoing Ebola outbreak, which is now recognized as the fastest growing on record. As of the latest updates, there have been 4,381 confirmed cases across five provinces. The outbreak reportedly began months before it was officially declared in May, complicating response efforts due to factors such as rebel conflict and infrastructure challenges.

stories.title: Trump's Secret Plane Switch in Turkey Amid Iran Threat
stories.summary: During a NATO summit in Turkey, President Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One to a military jet due to an assassination threat from Iran. Reports indicate that he was transported in a catering truck while the press was misled to believe he was still aboard Air Force One. This operation was described as an elaborate ruse to ensure his safety.

stories.title: Trump Issues Executive Order to Alter Childhood Vaccine Recommendations
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order that modifies childhood vaccination recommendations by limiting the inoculation schedule to 11 vaccines and advocating for spacing out vaccinations. The order aims to provide parents with more choices, but health experts and pediatricians have expressed concerns that these changes could lead to confusion and increased vulnerability among children.

stories.title: Iran Sets Six Conditions for U.S. to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has outlined six demands that the U.S. must meet to cease attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, President Trump has instructed his representatives to seek reparations from Iran, complicating negotiations further. The exchange of demands has led to rising oil prices and U.S. bond yields, indicating increased market tension.

stories.title: Trump Demands Compensation from Iran Amid Strait of Hormuz Stalemate
stories.summary: President Trump has demanded that Iran pay compensation for the deaths of U.S. soldiers and Iranian civilians, as negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have stalled. This demand reflects a deepening stalemate between the U.S. and Iran, with Trump asserting U.S. control over the strategic waterway. The situation has escalated as hopes for a deal fade.

stories.title: Death Toll Rises to 220 Following 7.4 Magnitude Earthquake in Colombia
stories.summary: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, resulting in at least 220 confirmed deaths and widespread destruction. The epicenter was located near San José del Palmar, approximately 250 miles from Bogotá. Rescue efforts are ongoing, with over 2,700 individuals reported missing as teams race to find survivors in the rubble.

stories.title: Trial for Tupac Shakur's Murder Begins Nearly 30 Years Later
stories.summary: The trial of Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, accused of orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, has commenced in Las Vegas. Jury selection began this week, nearly three decades after Shakur was fatally shot in a drive-by incident. Davis, who has pleaded not guilty, faces a potential life sentence without parole if convicted.

stories.title: Thai Prime Minister Suspends Firearm Licences Following School Shooting
stories.summary: In response to a recent school shooting, Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has suspended all firearms licences. This decision comes as the bodies of the teenage shooter and his grandparents, whom he killed, were cremated. The Prime Minister also emphasized the need for stricter controls and harsher penalties for firearms-related offenses.
